events.text: The Sky Rift has widened again over the outer Isles, and every small sect between the great courts is counting its gates and its stones. Cloud-couriers fly twice a day. Nobody on the White Stairs speaks of {ihw_war} aloud, and nobody speaks of anything else.

choices.text: Read the courier-slips and keep your counsel

effects.log: You read all of them. By dusk you know which small isles will bend first.

choices.text: Send the small sects a word of courage

effects.log: It costs you nothing and means little. They remember it anyway.

events.text: Word runs along the Sea of Clouds that {ihw_war} has begun. The great pavilions are shuttering their windows. The little sects on the drifting isles are ringing their wardens' bells and asking one another, without answers, whose banner will come first.

choices.text: Walk the lanes of the lesser isles and listen

effects.log: People tell you more than they tell the Ministries. You come home with a clearer map.

choices.text: Stay in your pavilion and cultivate

effects.log: The war will arrive without your help. You use the quiet well.

events.text: {ihw_house} has gone under the banner of {ihw_by}. The isle's lantern-gates were opened one night and the wardens did not fight. Refugees are rowing cloud-skiffs toward the outer stairs, and someone has told them your pavilion has room.

choices.text: Send aid to the fallen isle

effects.log: You send stones, silk and a letter. The isle will not forget who wrote it.

choices.text: Take in those who escaped

effects.log: Forty souls climb your stairs by morning, thin and grateful. Your name for mercy travels faster than they did.

choices.text: Let the isle go its own way

effects.log: It is not your isle. You tell yourself so, twice.

events.text: Under the Sky Rift's red glow, {ihw_house} yields to {ihw_by}. The old head signs with a shaking brush. Their disciples drift in scattered clouds across the Isles, and one of them is standing at your gate with a bundle and a bowed head.

choices.text: Send what stones and cloud-silk you can spare

effects.log: The parcel leaves before dawn, unmarked, though the recipients know whose seal was cut from it.

choices.text: Open the gate and take them in

effects.log: You give the exiles a wing of the pavilion. Within the season they have swept every step.

choices.text: Send the disciple on toward a farther isle

effects.log: You give directions and a cup of tea. It is all that you give.

events.text: A cloud-herald of {ihw_by} lands on your terrace with the banner furled under one arm. {ihw_war} has reached your own gate, the herald says, and the gate will bend or be bent. The herald says it with a pleasant smile, which is somehow the worst part.

choices.text: Hold the gate, and say so

effects.log: You tell the herald to take your answer back along the clouds. It sounds braver aloud than it feels in the dark.

choices.text: Bend, and keep the pavilion standing

effects.log: You sign. The war passes you over. The isles remember what the signature cost.

choices.text: Fly out and meet their host above the Rift

ok.log: You meet the van over the cloud-bank and turn it back. The banner retreats, and your gate stays yours.

fail.log: The van is stronger than it looked. You return battered, with the herald smile still waiting at the gate.

events.text: The host of {ihw_by} hangs over the Isles like weather, and a messenger arrives at dawn with terms written on a jade slip. Bend the gate, pay the tithe of stones, fly the banner beside your own. The slip adds that this is a courtesy, extended once.

choices.text: Refuse the terms

effects.log: You snap the slip across your knee and hand the halves back. The messenger bows exactly as deeply as courtesy demands.

choices.text: Accept the terms

effects.log: You press your seal to the slip. The host drifts onward, and the quiet that follows has a bitter taste.

choices.text: Answer the terms on the cloud-bank itself

ok.log: Your answer is written in qi across the sky. The host reconsiders its courtesy and moves on.

fail.log: The host does not move on. You fly home hurt, with the slip still unanswered in your sleeve.

events.text: Years later you pass the drifting place where {ihw_house} once stood. The isle is gone, scattered by {ihw_war}, and only a few weathered cloud-stones mark where the gate was. A crane circles once, and flies on.

choices.text: Leave a cup of tea on the last stone

effects.log: It is a small rite. The wind takes the steam, and you take the road.

choices.text: Fly on without stopping

effects.log: You do not look down. Some places are better carried than visited.

events.text: Someone in the Jade Court's tea-house asks whether you remember {ihw_house}. You do. It is gone now, its slips scattered, its wardens lost in the long war. The asker has no more to say. You find that you do.

choices.text: Tell them what the isle was like

effects.log: You speak until the lamps burn low. Two strangers write down what you remember.

choices.text: Say it was long ago and change the subject

effects.log: You change it. The tea tastes like ash for a while.

events.text: {ihw_house} is not what it was. After {ihw_war} it kept the banner of {ihw_by} by choice, and now its wardens bow to strangers and smile at you with careful teeth. They invite you to tea. The tea is excellent and the conversation is a test.

choices.text: Drink, and say nothing of the old days

effects.log: You are polite and empty. They learn nothing, and neither do you.

choices.text: Speak plainly of what they have become

effects.log: The tea cools. Nobody argues, and nobody forgives you either.

events.text: The old sect gate on the small isle now bears two banners, one of them yours to remember and one it should not be flying. {ihw_house} chose this, the wardens say, and chose it freely. You were not asked to forgive it, only to see it.

choices.text: Walk through the gate and see it all

effects.log: The courtyard is clean and quiet. Only the gate-guards avoid your eyes.

choices.text: Turn back at the threshold

effects.log: Some doors you decline to walk through, even when they are open.

events.text: A head of {ihw_house} that nobody knew has risen from the wreck of {ihw_war}: a quiet cultivator who had never held a post. The isle drifts back toward the Sea of Clouds under new management, and an invitation to the first banquet reaches you.

choices.text: Attend, and take the measure of the stranger

effects.log: The new head is sharper than the old, and kinder than expected. You leave with a good impression.

choices.text: Send a gift and stay home

effects.log: The gift is accepted with a note of careful, correct thanks.

events.text: Nobody on the Isles can say who now leads {ihw_house}. The old head is gone, the heirs dispersed, and some unremarked disciple has gathered the pieces. They come to your pavilion in plain grey, bow, and ask for nothing but a name written in your register.

choices.text: Write the name, and pour tea

effects.log: The guest drinks it in silence. Something small begins here, as small things do.

choices.text: Ask for proof of the claim before writing anything

effects.log: The proof is thin but honest. You write the name after all.

events.text: {ihw_house} comes back from {ihw_war} with fewer disciples and harder faces. The stairs are swept at dawn by hands that do not tremble. When you visit, nobody asks for anything. The wardens are past asking.

choices.text: Leave a quiet gift at the gate

effects.log: You leave stones and silk with no name on it. The wardens know anyway.

choices.text: Greet the head and keep it brief

effects.log: The head returns your bow with the exact depth of a debt paid.

events.text: The little isle of {ihw_house} drifts back into sight, leaner now, its disciples drilling in the mist before dawn. {ihw_war} took their softness and left their discipline behind. They have no patience for visitors and no complaints for the sky.

choices.text: Watch the drill from a distance

effects.log: It is a fine drill. It is also a warning to anyone who has not yet noticed.

choices.text: Send a courier with congratulations

effects.log: The courier returns with one word, which is thanks, and nothing more.

events.text: Against all expectation {ihw_house} emerges from {ihw_war} unchanged. The same bells ring, the same tea steams, the same old warden grumbles on the same stair. You almost envy the stillness.

choices.text: Stay a night and enjoy the quiet

effects.log: Nothing happens, wonderfully. You depart rested.

choices.text: Ask how they came through untouched

effects.log: The old warden shrugs. Luck, discretion, a good cook. You write down the name of the cook.

events.text: The small sect {ihw_house} drifts home after {ihw_war} looking exactly as it did before. It makes you wonder what the war was for. A disciple waves at you from the terrace, and you wave back, and that is all.

choices.text: Wave back and move on

effects.log: Some things are simple. You let this be one.

choices.text: Climb the stair and share a cup

effects.log: You exchange gossip over the same chipped cups. Nothing of consequence is said.

events.text: {ihw_house} returns from {ihw_war} with an old memory in every disciple's eye: that you once sent aid. The head meets you at the gate with both hands raised in the old greeting. "Our doors are yours," they say. "We do not forget."

choices.text: Accept the welcome gladly

effects.log: They give you the best seat and the oldest tea. A friendship that cost little pays back much.

choices.text: Ask only that they look after the next in need

effects.log: The head promises it. The promise is kept for a long while.

events.text: The isle you helped through {ihw_war}, {ihw_house}, has come home and wants you to know it. They send cloud-silk, a jar of their best tea, and a letter that says only: you came when it mattered, and we came back. You read it twice.

choices.text: Write back a short, warm word

effects.log: The reply is brief. The friendship that follows is not.

choices.text: Visit in person and see how they fare

effects.log: The isle has healed more than you expected. They show you every repaired stair.

events.text: A lantern-keeper of {ihw_house} arrives alone at your mooring in a skiff that is more patch than hull. The isle has fallen to {ihw_by}; its sky-bridges were taken down before dawn. She carries the great gate-lantern wrapped in her sleeves, still lit. She says nothing of mercy. She asks only where on your isle a lantern may be hung.

choices.text: Send stones and cloud-silk to the fallen isle, and hang its lantern in your hall

effects.log: The lantern burns above your stairs for a century. The silk reaches those left behind.

choices.text: Offer the lantern-keeper and her kin the empty east wing

effects.log: Thirty come, thin and quiet, and the lantern is hung by the east door. Your isle gains a reputation, and a nursery.

choices.text: Direct her to a larger isle with deeper stores

effects.log: She bows, and the skiff slips away downwind, lantern shining. You tell yourself it was practical.

events.text: The banner of {ihw_by} drops from a dawn cloud onto your landing, carried by a herald with a flute at his belt and three archers behind. {ihw_war} has reached the gates of your isle, he says, and offers terms between phrases of a tune. The archers keep their bows low, politely. The flute plays a very slow, very reasonable note.

choices.text: Tell the herald the gates stay shut

effects.log: He plays the answer back as a rising line and nods. The archers lower their bows another inch, in respect or in mockery.

choices.text: Accept the terms, and have the banner hung beside yours

effects.log: The flute rests. The banner is hung. The isle remembers it, quietly, like a draught under a door.

choices.text: Fly up into the cloud and meet the archers face to face

ok.log: You break their line above the cloud-bank and the banner withdraws, flute silent. Your gate remains yours.

fail.log: The archers are better than they looked. You limp home with the flute's last note still sounding in your ears.

events.text: The War in Heaven has reached the borders of the minor pantheons. Every small temple-god between the great thrones is counting shrines and faithful. Messenger-birds cross the sky in double flocks, and nobody at the Heavenly Court will say the word {ihw_war} in a normal voice.

choices.text: Read the dispatches and keep your counsel

effects.log: You read them all. By evening you know which small pantheons will bow first.

choices.text: Send the lesser gods a word of courage

effects.log: It costs you only a breath. They carry it into the dark and are glad.

events.text: News passes from altar to altar that {ihw_war} is upon the heavens. The great pantheons shutter their halls. The small ones light every votive lamp they own and ask whose banner will cross their threshold first.

choices.text: Visit the lesser shrines and listen

effects.log: The small gods tell you things the great ones never would. You return with a clearer map.

choices.text: Keep to your sanctum and deepen your rites

effects.log: The war will come regardless of your presence. You use the stillness well.

events.text: {ihw_house} has fallen under the banner of {ihw_by}. Its temple doors were opened by night and its guardians stood aside. Dispossessed godlings are trekking toward your border shrines, and one of them carries the old seal of the fallen pantheon.

choices.text: Send offerings to the fallen pantheon

effects.log: You send incense, grain and a tablet blessed in your name. The fallen will remember who sent it.

choices.text: Shelter the godlings who escaped

effects.log: A dozen small gods find room in your shrines. Your name for mercy crosses the heavens ahead of them.

choices.text: Let the pantheon meet its own fate

effects.log: It is not yours to rescue. You repeat that on the way to your altar.

events.text: {ihw_house} bows to {ihw_by} beneath a sky streaked with divine fire. Its elder god signs a covenant with a trembling hand. The smaller deities scatter like startled doves, and one of them kneels at your temple steps without a word.

choices.text: Send offerings and a blessing in aid

effects.log: The parcel departs before dawn, unsigned, though everyone can guess whose censer filled it.

choices.text: Open the temple doors to the refugees

effects.log: You give them an east wing. Within the month the steps are swept and the lamps trimmed.

choices.text: Point the kneeling god toward a distant shrine

effects.log: You offer a direction and a cup of nectar. That is all you offer.

events.text: A herald of {ihw_by} descends to your temple court with the banner rolled under one arm. {ihw_war} has reached your own sanctum, the herald says, and your gate must bend or be bent. The herald is smiling, which somehow makes it worse.

choices.text: Hold your temple and say so

effects.log: You tell the herald to carry your answer home on its own wings. It sounds braver aloud than it feels.

choices.text: Bend, and keep the temple standing

effects.log: You sign. The war passes you by. The heavens remember what the signature cost.

choices.text: Ascend and meet their host in the open sky

roll.foeName: The host in the open sky

ok.log: You meet the van above the clouds and turn it back. The banner retreats and your gate remains yours.

fail.log: The van is mightier than it looked. You descend scorched, with the herald smile still waiting in your court.

events.text: The host of {ihw_by} fills the horizon of the heavens, and at dawn a messenger lays terms on your altar, written on gold leaf. Open the sanctum, give the tithe of faith, hang the banner beside your own. This is a courtesy, the leaf notes, extended once.

choices.text: Refuse the terms

effects.log: You fold the leaf in two and hand it back. The messenger bows precisely as deep as protocol requires.

choices.text: Accept the terms

effects.log: You press your sigil to the leaf. The host drifts on, and the silence afterwards tastes of tin.

choices.text: Answer the terms in person above the temple

roll.foeName: The host in the open sky

ok.log: Your answer is written in light across the vault of heaven. The host reconsiders its courtesy and turns elsewhere.

fail.log: The host does not turn. You retreat wounded, the leaf still unanswered in your hand.

events.text: Ages later you pass the place where the pantheon of {ihw_house} once stood. It was unmade in {ihw_war}, and only a few cracked altar-stones mark where its doors were. A dove circles once, and wings on.

choices.text: Leave an offering on the last altar

effects.log: A small rite. The wind lifts the incense, and you take your road.

choices.text: Pass by without stopping

effects.log: You do not look down. Some places are better remembered than revisited.

events.text: A god at a divine banquet asks whether you remember {ihw_house}. You do. Its shrines are dust, its faithful scattered, its name nearly gone from the Book of Fates. The asker has nothing more to say. You find you do.

choices.text: Tell them what that pantheon was like

effects.log: You speak until the lamps gutter. Two young gods write down what you remember.

choices.text: Say it was ages ago and change the subject

effects.log: You change it. The nectar tastes of ash for a while.

effects.log: The feast cools. Nobody argues, and nobody forgives you either.

choices.text: Walk through the gate and see it all

effects.log: The court is spotless and quiet. Only the gate-keepers avoid your eyes.

choices.text: Turn back at the threshold

effects.log: Some doors you decline to enter, even when they stand open.

effects.log: The new head is sharper than the old, and kinder than expected. You leave impressed.

choices.text: Send a gift and stay home

effects.log: The gift is accepted with a note of careful, correct thanks.

effects.log: The guest drinks in silence. Something small begins here, as small things do.

effects.log: The proof is thin but honest. You enter the name after all.

effects.log: You leave grain and incense with no name on it. The priests know anyway.

effects.log: The head returns your bow with the exact depth of a debt repaid.

effects.log: It is a fine rite. It is also a warning to anyone who has not yet noticed.

effects.log: The messenger returns with one word, which is thanks, and nothing more.

effects.log: Nothing happens, wonderfully. You depart rested.

effects.log: The old priest shrugs. Luck, discretion, a good cook. You write down the name of the cook.

choices.text: Wave back and move on

effects.log: Some things are simple. You let this be one.

effects.log: You exchange gossip over the same chipped cups. Nothing of consequence is said.

choices.text: Accept the welcome gladly

effects.log: They give you the best seat and the oldest nectar. A friendship that cost little pays back much.

choices.text: Ask only that they shelter the next in need

effects.log: The head promises it. The promise is kept for a long while.

events.text: The pantheon you helped through {ihw_war}, {ihw_house}, has come home and wants you to know it. They send sacred cloth, a jar of their best ambrosia, and a message that says only: you came when it mattered, and we came back. You read it twice.

choices.text: Send back a short, warm word

effects.log: The reply is brief. The friendship that follows is not.

choices.text: Visit in person and see how they fare

effects.log: The temples have healed more than you expected. They show you every repaired altar.

events.text: The shrine-lamps of {ihw_house} went out in a single night when {ihw_by} took the altar. A bell-ringer, last of its priests, climbs the steps of your temple with the clapper of the old bell wrapped in her apron. She does not beg. She asks only whether there is a hook in your belfry on which it might hang, until the faithful of her god return.

choices.text: Send offerings to the fallen shrine and hang the clapper in your belfry

effects.log: The clapper hangs where it can be seen. Pilgrims from the fallen domain light a taper at it, and bless you without knowing.

choices.text: Open the cloister to the bell-ringer and her faithful

effects.log: Thirty pilgrims come, and the clapper is hung. Within the season your belfry has a new voice, flat and cheerful.

choices.text: Point her to a larger temple with a larger belfry

effects.log: She thanks you, and goes. The apron is the last thing you see, a pale shape on the road.

events.text: An envoy of {ihw_by} enters your court at noon, preceded by a boy with a gong, and unrolls a scroll of gold leaf. {ihw_war} has come to your domain, it reads, and offers the kind of friendship that comes with a standing garrison. The envoy reads it all in a good voice, pausing for the gong, like a man announcing a feast.

choices.text: Strike the gong yourself, and say the temple stays as it is

effects.log: The note is wide and clean. The envoy folds the scroll and says it will be noted in the proper registry.

choices.text: Sign in the margin, and house the garrison

effects.log: You sign. The gong sounds, and the garrison moves in. Your faithful look at the new banner, and at you.

choices.text: Meet the envoy's escort on the temple steps, and answer them there

roll.foeName: The host in the open sky

ok.log: The escort is turned back on the steps, gong and all. The envoy withdraws with the scroll furled very tightly.

fail.log: The escort is stronger than the scroll let on. You are carried indoors by your own acolytes, and the gong sounds once more, softly.

events.text: The wells in the valley have started to taste of iron, and the old women say that means {ihw_war}. Peddlers carry the same news from three different directions and each swears it is only a rumour. Shutters close early. The little houses that once squabbled over the water-rights now meet at the crossroads and talk, for the first time in your memory, in low voices.

choices.text: Sit at the crossroads and hear all of them out

effects.log: It is a long evening. You head home knowing whose granary is empty and whose gate has no bolt.

choices.text: Write a short letter to every house that you can reach

effects.log: The letters are brief and plain. They are answered with thanks, and with fear.

events.text: A shepherd runs down from the pass with his crook in one hand and his hat in the other: {ihw_war} is on the far side of the hills, and the lamps of the hill-forts are going out one by one. At the mill nobody talks about the harvest. The little schools lock their courtyards. Children are called in from the fields in the middle of the afternoon.

choices.text: Go up the pass yourself and look

effects.log: You look. You see enough to be useful and little enough to sleep.

choices.text: Stay home and keep to your forms

effects.log: You practise by lamplight. What comes will find you better than it would have.

events.text: {ihw_house} has taken the colours of {ihw_by}. They did it at night, with the miller holding the gate. Now a line of carts creaks up your lane, loaded with bedding and caged hens, and the lead driver, a woman with a baby strapped to her back, asks whether your barn is still empty.

choices.text: Load a cart with flour and blankets and send it down

effects.log: The cart rolls out at dawn. The woman writes your name on the lid with a burnt stick.

choices.text: Open the barn and light the stove

effects.log: Forty people sleep in the straw that night, and nobody asks who pays. By spring they have mended your roof.

choices.text: Tell them the next town is bigger and has a better barn

effects.log: They nod and drive on. You stand at the gate until the dust settles, then stay a while longer.

events.text: You hear it from a tinker: {ihw_house} has bowed to {ihw_by}. The old master signed, they say, with his left hand because the right would not hold the brush. A young apprentice from there is already sitting on your doorstep, boots wrapped in sacking, holding a bundle of schoolbooks tied with twine. She will not look up.

choices.text: Pack a sack of oats and cloth and send it after the others

effects.log: The sack goes with the carrier, no name on it. The old master hears whose twine it was tied with.

choices.text: Open the door and take the apprentice in

effects.log: You give her the loft and a stool by the fire. Inside the month she is teaching the village children their letters.

choices.text: Give her bread and the way to the coast road

effects.log: You give her all of it. It is not much, and she thanks you as though it were.

events.text: A courier of {ihw_by} dismounts at your gate and unrolls a banner that is not his own, to show you what yours will look like. {ihw_war} has reached your valley, he says, and there are two kinds of gate: the one that bends and the one that gets bent. He smiles throughout. His horse crops your hedge.

choices.text: Tell him your gate stays as it is

effects.log: You say it plainly. He tilts his head, writes it in a small book, and leads his horse out of your hedge.

choices.text: Sign the paper, and keep the roof over your people

effects.log: You sign. The war walks round you. The valley remembers what the ink cost.

choices.text: Go out and meet their foot-soldiers at the mill ford

ok.log: You meet the van in the shallows and turn it. The banner drifts upstream, and the gate is still yours.

fail.log: Their van is more than it looked. You are carried home wet and bruised, and the courier's smile has waited.

events.text: A drum sounds in the valley before dawn and does not stop. By the time the cocks crow, {ihw_by} has camped on the common, and an under-officer with ink on his thumbs has pinned terms to your gate: open the road, feed the camp, fly a second flag. It says the offer is made in friendship, and that friendship is perishable.

choices.text: Pull down the terms and send them back in pieces

effects.log: You return them in pieces, tied with string. The under-officer thanks you for the string.

choices.text: Accept, and send over the first cartload of feed

effects.log: The camp eats and moves on. The drum stops. Your neighbours do not speak of it, for years.

choices.text: Go to the common and give your answer in person

ok.log: Your answer is short and loud. The camp strikes its tents and goes elsewhere, muttering about hospitality.

fail.log: The camp does not go. You limp home with the terms still unanswered in your coat.

events.text: Years on, you take a different road to market and find yourself at the mound where {ihw_house} stood. Nettles cover the foundations. A well, uncovered, still has its rope. The records say {ihw_war} took it, and the records are usually right. A swallow nests in what was the schoolroom window.

choices.text: Draw a bucket from the well and pour it on the doorstep

effects.log: The water darkens the stone. You walk home feeling an odd sort of tidiness.

choices.text: Move on before the light fails

effects.log: You move on. Some places are better remembered than revisited.

events.text: A weaver at the fair tells you, while her hands go on working, that her mother came from {ihw_house}. She has the pattern of the gate-cloth in her head. She can't read the old school name, but she weaves it into every hem. She asks if you knew the place. Behind her the loom clacks like a heart.

choices.text: Tell her everything you remember, and what it smelled like

effects.log: You talk for an hour. She writes none of it down, and forgets none of it.

choices.text: Say you only passed through once, and ask about the cloth

effects.log: She takes the hint and turns the talk to thread. The hem stays in your mind.

events.text: {ihw_house} survived {ihw_war} and flies the flag of {ihw_by} still, and its old masters are fatter and politer for it. They invite you to the autumn feast and seat you between a magistrate and a plump cousin. Every dish has been chosen with care. Every glance across the table is a small question.

choices.text: Eat well, and tell no stories of the old days

effects.log: You are agreeable and empty. They learn nothing, and neither do you.

choices.text: Raise your cup and say what you see

effects.log: The feast cools. No one argues, and no one forgives you either.

events.text: On the gate of {ihw_house} two flags hang side by side now, its own and a newer one. A fresh-faced porter explains, without being asked, that they chose it themselves after the war. They are very clear about the word chose. He does not ask you to approve. He only holds the gate wide open and waits.

choices.text: Walk in and look at everything

effects.log: The yard is spotless. Nobody there will quite meet your eye.

choices.text: Stop on the step, and turn back

effects.log: Some gates you decline to cross, even open.

events.text: Someone nobody had heard of now speaks for {ihw_house}: a quiet cousin who spent {ihw_war} mending nets two valleys over. The old line is gone. The house is alive again under a new roof-beam, and a card of invitation, in careful square letters, reaches your table for its first harvest supper.

choices.text: Go to the supper and take stock of the new head

effects.log: The cousin is sharper than the last head and kinder than expected. You leave with a good impression.

choices.text: Send a basket of apples and stay home

effects.log: The thanks come back in the same square letters, and do not say a word too many.

events.text: The rolls of {ihw_house} are blank after {ihw_war}, and the man who now sits at the old writing-desk does not claim any name at all. He knocks at your door with a lamp, in plain wool, and asks only that you write a line in your own hand to say you know him. He sets the lamp on your sill and waits.

choices.text: Write the line, and put the kettle on

effects.log: He drinks his tea in silence. Something small begins in the kitchen that night, as small things do.

choices.text: Ask a few questions first, and then write it

effects.log: The answers are thin but honest. You write the line anyway.

events.text: {ihw_house} comes home from {ihw_war} with half its faces gone and the rest set like stone. The yard is raked at dawn by hands that do not tremble. At the gate there is no bell, no greeting, no bowl of tea. Nobody asks a thing of you. They are past asking, and most of the village keeps its distance.

choices.text: Leave a sack of grain by the gate without a mark

effects.log: No one thanks you aloud. Next market day the sack comes back, full of dried herbs.

choices.text: Bow to the head and keep it short

effects.log: The head returns the bow to the exact inch. It is the bow of a settled debt.

events.text: The ruined school of {ihw_house} rises again on its hill, and the pupils drill in the fog before the cocks wake. {ihw_war} took the softness out of them and left the discipline. Visitors are not welcome. The pupils do not look at the road. Their breath rises in thin white lines, in step, and their teacher counts without a sound.

choices.text: Stand at the road's edge and watch the drill

effects.log: It is a very fine drill. It is also a plain warning to anyone who has not yet noticed.

choices.text: Send a boy with a basket and a short note

effects.log: The boy returns with a single word: thanks.

events.text: {ihw_house} comes through {ihw_war} untouched, as if the war had walked around it in a wide circle. The same mill-wheel turns. The same hen scratches by the same step. Someone has painted the gate a brighter blue. You find yourself envying a stillness you had not known you wanted.

choices.text: Stay the night and sleep soundly

effects.log: Nothing happens, gloriously. You leave rested, with a jar of honey.

choices.text: Ask the old gatekeeper how they were passed over

effects.log: He shrugs. Good luck, a patient cook, and an unmemorable name. You write the cook's name down.

events.text: When you arrive at {ihw_house} after {ihw_war}, it looks exactly as you left it, down to the cracked step and the lopsided scarecrow. Even the dog is the same. You wonder what the whole business was for. A girl waves from the roof-ridge, and you wave back, and that is the whole of it.

choices.text: Wave and go on your way

effects.log: Some things are simple. You let this one be.

choices.text: Go in and share a cup of tea with whoever is there

effects.log: You trade gossip over the same chipped cups. Nothing of weight is said, and it does you good.

events.text: When {ihw_house} comes out of {ihw_war}, the first folk you see at the crossroads are its people, arms spread, calling your name in the old greeting. They remember the cart of flour you sent. "Our door is yours," says the head, wiping her eyes. "We have kept the best chair for you."

choices.text: Take the chair and the story that goes with it

effects.log: They give you the oldest tea and the warmest corner. A kindness that cost you little returns a great deal.

choices.text: Ask only that they do the same for the next one in need

effects.log: The head promises, and the promise is kept for a good long time.

events.text: A basket comes up your lane from {ihw_house}, borne by two children who set it on your step and run. Inside: a cheese, a bottle of plum brandy, and a letter that reads, in a hand you now know: you came when it counted, and we came back. You read it twice, and then you read the cheese, which is, as it turns out, very good.

choices.text: Send a short, warm reply and a jar of your own pickles

effects.log: The pickles are praised for a year. The friendship that follows is less loud, and longer.

choices.text: Walk over and see how the place has mended

effects.log: The fences are up, the schoolroom is warm. They show you every repaired board with pride.
